title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Plastering
audience: Plasterers and plastering contractors, including solo operators, who quote for room replasters, wall and ceiling repairs and mixed plaster-and-paint jobs.
learningOutcomes: Write a plastering offer with a clear finish, a time frame, the client's tasks and a guarantee
Identify the friction and risk a homeowner, builder or landlord carries and reduce them
Price a plastering job on value and cost, not only on hours

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will plaster your walls' is a service. 'I will replaster the lounge walls and ceiling, leave them flat to the agreed finish, and give you a drying window before any paint goes on, with a level check and photos at sign-off' is an offer. The client is buying a flat, sound wall that is ready to decorate, and the certainty that the job will not leave cracks or bulges behind.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: State the outcome: the surfaces, the plaster type, and the finish standard. Set a time frame in working days, including the drying time before the next trade. List what the client must do, such as clearing the room, moving fixtures and confirming access and power. Add one certainty element, such as a level check at sign-off and photos. Name the risk you carry, such as a fix-first window for cracks that you caused. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, for example electrical work, moisture repairs, or painting, because a written quote becomes binding once accepted (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes, last updated 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make the booking, access and handover simple. A scope sheet, a fixed start day, a clear drying window and an agreed tidy-up at the end of each day each remove a decision or a worry for the client. A client who knows when the wall is ready for paint and who does what next will value the offer more. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the client usually support a higher price, because the client is paying for certainty and reliability.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and workmanship
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services and cannot be excluded by contract, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds, last updated 27 May 2025). A written workmanship warranty is an optional promise that sits on top of those guarantees. In Victoria, a business is generally given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault at no charge (Consumer Victoria, Services not done with due care and skill, last updated 13 October 2023). That page does not set a fix-window length, so choose your own window and check its cost before you publish it. Make the guarantee's limits clear, such as what happens if the substrate moves or moisture is present behind the wall, and confirm those limits with your own insurer or adviser.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the finish and the risk, then check the price against cost and time. A higher price is easier to defend when the client can see the preparation, the finish standard and the saved time. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin, so check the price against cost before adding any premium (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes). Stepped packages, for example a patch repair, a single room, or a full room with ceiling and a paint line, let the client see what each step adds (Jobber Academy, Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). That source is an older, general service article and not plastering data. Show one clear total and say whether GST is included, as WA Consumer Protection asks for WA quotes (updated 4 September 2026).

procedure: Write the finished result for the room or wall in one sentence a client would repeat.
Set a time frame in working days, including drying time before the next trade, and record how often past jobs met it.
List what the client must do, such as clearing the room, moving fixtures and confirming access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a level check at sign-off or photos.
Decide the fix-first and guarantee terms, and check that you can afford them.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A plasterer quotes an hourly rate for a full-room replaster and loses jobs to lower quotes. Clients say they cannot tell what the finished wall will look like or when they can paint it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer and decide how to price it.
workedExamples.reasoning: A fixed-scope offer that names the surfaces, the plaster type, the finish standard, the drying window and a fix-first period gives the client certainty that an hourly quote does not. One vendor listing gives a range of $1,500 to $4,000 or more for a full-room replaster (TradeRefer plastering page, undated, vendor listing, indicative only). Use that range only as a sense-check. The painter builds the price from the plasterer's own cost and hours. If the offer includes painting, state the painting as a separate line, because in Victoria plastering combined with painting is treated as mixed work that still needs registration. The Victorian sources read word the $10,000 threshold three ways ('more than $10,000', '$10,000 or more' and 'over $10,000'), so treat that threshold as unresolved and check it against the Victorian Act and with the Victorian Building Authority before use.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to what you control, such as a fix-first visit within a stated period, and cost that visit before you publish it.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate, such as a flatness standard you have not measured
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured or can show, and get the client's consent before using their photos.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Plastering work can need a licence or registration, and the job value and the mix of trades can decide it. In NSW, wet plastering needs a contractor licence for trade work valued over $5,000 in labour and materials including GST. Check the rules for the state where the work is done before you quote.
Pricing statements are covered by the Australian Consumer Law. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, Setting prices: what's allowed, last modified 15 July 2026).

qualityStandard: Every plastering offer is written down, with scope, exclusions, client tasks, drying window and the guarantee terms.
Offer and pricing decisions are checked against cost and time, and against the licence rule for the job value and trade mix in the state where the work is done.
documentationEvidence: Written plastering offer with scope, exclusions, drying window and fix-first terms
Dated cost and time check for the price
Evidence collected, such as level-check photos with the client's consent, and the decision made
summary: A plastering offer promises a flat, sound finish, a time frame, certainty and a fair guarantee.
A higher rate follows from clearer value, such as a defined finish and a clear drying window, not from longer hours.
Check the state licence rule for the job value and trade mix before you publish a price.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a plastering offer does the client buy?
options: Your hourly rate and your van
Your trowel collection and the brands you use
How many years you have been plastering

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a plastering guarantee or fix-first promise be?
options: Unlimited, with no end date and no defined scope
Something you can deliver and afford
Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a measurable claim about a finish, such as a stated flatness standard, have?

officialReferences.title: Prepare quotes (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says a written quote becomes binding once accepted and that a quote should recover cost plus a margin. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Warranties and refunds (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says an optional warranty sits on top of consumer guarantees, and that a no-refunds line does not override service rights. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: States that misleading price statements are prohibited. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Estimates, quotes and deposits (WA Consumer Protection)
officialReferences.covers: Western Australia only. Supports showing one total and whether GST is included, getting written approval before extra work, and a deposit generally no more than 10 per cent. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.
